Newton's law of universal gravitation

Words: 225 Articles: 9
Classical mechanics OurBigBook.com
Newton's law of universal gravitation states that two point masses attract one another with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.

Newtonian gravitational field

Words: 193 Articles: 8
Newton's law of universal gravitation OurBigBook.com
Outside a spherical mass M, the Newtonian gravitational field is radial and has magnitude
g(r)=r2GM​.
(1)

Gravitational acceleration (g)

Words: 35
Newtonian gravitational field OurBigBook.com
Gravitational acceleration is the acceleration of a freely falling test body in a gravitational field. Near Earth's surface its magnitude is approximately constant on shallow vertical scales, and is conventionally denoted by g.

Gravitational constant (G)

Words: 9
Newtonian gravitational field OurBigBook.com
The gravitational constant is the proportionality constant in Newton's law of universal gravitation.

Newtonian gravitational potential (Φ)

Words: 66 Articles: 2
Newtonian gravitational field OurBigBook.com
The Newtonian gravitational potential is the potential energy per unit test mass. Outside a spherical mass M it is Φ(r)=−GM/r after choosing zero at infinity, and the gravitational acceleration is −∇Φ.
Newtonian potential of a point mass (Φ(r)=−GM/r)
Words: 13
Newtonian gravitational potential OurBigBook.com
The free-space Green function of the Laplacian gives the Newtonian gravitational potential Φ(r)=−GM/r for a point mass M at the origin.
Spherically symmetric potential
Words: 21
Newtonian gravitational potential OurBigBook.com
A spherically symmetric potential depends only on distance r from one point. Its force is central, so angular momentum is conserved.

Newtonian gravitational potential energy

Words: 18
Newtonian gravitational field OurBigBook.com
Two point masses m1​,m2​ separated by distance r have potential energy
V(r)=−rGm1​m2​​.
(2)
The corresponding attractive force is −∇V.

Cavendish experiment

Words: 49 Articles: 1
Newtonian gravitational field OurBigBook.com
The Cavendish experiment measures the weak Newtonian gravitational field between laboratory masses with a torsion balance, and can be used to determine the gravitational constant.
Cavendish torsion balance
Words: 28
Cavendish experiment OurBigBook.com
A Cavendish torsion balance measures the small gravitational torque exerted by source masses on test masses mounted on a suspended rod. The fiber's twist reveals the horizontal force.

Degree of freedom

A degree of freedom is an independent coordinate needed to specify a mechanical configuration after all mechanical constraints have been imposed.

Mechanical constraint

Words: 16
Classical mechanics OurBigBook.com
A mechanical constraint restricts the allowed configurations or velocities of a system and reduces its degrees of freedom.

Position OurBigBook.com

Velocity

Speed

Velocity OurBigBook.com
Speed is the magnitude ∣v∣ of velocity.

Acceleration

Words: 6
Velocity OurBigBook.com
Acceleration is the time derivative of velocity.

Constant speed

Words: 16
Velocity OurBigBook.com
A trajectory has constant speed when the magnitude of its velocity does not vary with time.

Terminal velocity

Words: 17
Velocity OurBigBook.com
Terminal velocity is the constant limiting velocity reached when a velocity-dependent resistive force balances the applied force.

Momentum

Classical mechanics OurBigBook.com
For a nonrelativistic particle of mass m and velocity v, the momentum is p=mv.

Momentum conservation

Words: 32
Momentum OurBigBook.com
Momentum conservation states that the total momentum of an isolated system is constant. In a translation-invariant field theory, integrating over the spacetime zero mode enforces momentum conservation at interactions and scattering amplitudes.

Rocket equation

Words: 60 Articles: 1
Momentum OurBigBook.com
For a body of varying mass M ejecting material at fixed relative velocity, conservation of momentum gives a differential relation between dM and the body's change dv. Integrating it produces a logarithm of the mass ratio.

Forward-exhaust rocket equation

Words: 24
Rocket equation OurBigBook.com
If a vehicle moving at speed v ejects mass forward at relative speed u>0, then
Mdv=udM.
(3)
As dM<0, the vehicle slows down.

Angular momentum (L)

Momentum OurBigBook.com
The angular momentum of a particle about the origin is L=r×p.

Conservation of angular momentum

Words: 46 Articles: 1
Angular momentum OurBigBook.com
The total angular momentum of an isolated system is constant. More generally, its time derivative equals the external torque.
Central-force radial turning point
Words: 27
Conservation of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
For unit mass in a central force with potential Φ(r) and conserved angular momentum L, a radial turning point r∗​ has zero radial speed and therefore satisfies
E=2r∗2​L2​+Φ(r∗​).
(4)

Angular momentum transport

Words: 28
Angular momentum OurBigBook.com
Angular momentum transport moves angular momentum between locations through matter, stresses, waves, or fields. An accretion disk must transport angular momentum outward for most of its mass to move inward.

Torque (τ)

Words: 42 Articles: 1
Angular momentum OurBigBook.com
Torque is the moment of force, τ=r×F, and equals the rate of change of angular momentum.
Moment balance
Words: 24
Torque OurBigBook.com
Moment balance equates the rate of change of angular momentum to applied torques. A static slender rod obeys ∂s​M+t×F+m=0.

Areal velocity (A˙)

Words: 27
Angular momentum OurBigBook.com
The areal velocity is the rate at which the radius vector sweeps area. For specific angular momentum h, it is constant and equals
A˙=21​r2θ˙=2h​.
(5)

Energy

Energy is a conserved scalar quantity associated with time-translation symmetry.

Energy function

Energy OurBigBook.com
For a Lagrangian L(q,q˙​,t), its energy function is
E=∑i​q˙​i​∂q˙​i​∂L​−L.
(6)
It is conserved along Euler-Lagrange trajectories when L has no explicit time dependence.

Mechanical energy (E=T+V)

Words: 24
Energy OurBigBook.com
Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy. It is conserved when all forces are conservative and the potential has no explicit time dependence.

Work

Energy OurBigBook.com
The work done by a force along a path is W=∫F⋅dr.

Work-energy theorem

Words: 11
Work OurBigBook.com
The net work on a particle equals its change in kinetic energy:
∫ab​F⋅dr=Δ(21​mv2).
(7)

Power

Work OurBigBook.com
Power is the rate of energy transfer, P=dW/dt.

Kinetic energy

Energy OurBigBook.com
The nonrelativistic kinetic energy of a particle is T=mv2/2.

Kinetic energy density

Words: 30
Kinetic energy OurBigBook.com
The kinetic energy density of a continuum with mass density ρ and velocity v is ρ∣v∣2/2. For a displacement field, the material velocity is its time derivative.

Rotational kinetic energy (K=21​Iω2)

Words: 22
Kinetic energy OurBigBook.com
A rigid body rotating about a fixed axis with moment of inertia I and angular speed ω has kinetic energy K=Iω2/2.

Potential energy

Words: 199 Articles: 8
Energy OurBigBook.com
A conservative force is the negative gradient of a potential energy: F=−∇V.

Potential function

Words: 27
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
A potential function V assigns a scalar to each point of a configuration or spatial domain. In mechanics it represents potential energy, and its negative gradient gives the corresponding conservative force.

Central potential

Words: 26
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
A central potential depends only on distance from a fixed centre, V(x)=V(∣x∣). Its force is radial, and rotational symmetry implies conservation of angular momentum.

Conservative force

Words: 52 Articles: 1
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
A force is conservative when its work depends only on the endpoints. On a simply connected domain this is equivalent to F=−∇V for a potential energy V.
Nonconservative force
Words: 25
Conservative force OurBigBook.com
A nonconservative force has path-dependent work. On a simply connected domain, a continuously differentiable force is nonconservative exactly when its curl does not vanish identically.

Inverse-square potential (V(r)=−k/r)

Words: 10
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
The potential V(r)=−k/r generates the attractive inverse-square central force F=−kr/r3.

Exponential cusp potential

Words: 30
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
The even potential
V(x)=V∞​(1−e−∣x∣/λ)
(8)
has a cusp at the origin and approaches the finite value V∞​. Motions below that value oscillate between symmetric turning points; motions above it escape.

Escape velocity

Words: 15
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
Escape velocity is the least initial speed whose total energy permits motion to spatial infinity.

Equipotential surface

Words: 25
Potential energy OurBigBook.com
An equipotential surface is a level set of a scalar potential. Its gradient and the corresponding conservative force are normal to every smooth level surface.

Turning point

Words: 23
Energy OurBigBook.com
A turning point of one-dimensional motion is a position where the kinetic energy and instantaneous velocity vanish before the direction of motion reverses.

Period of an oscillation (T)

Words: 15
Classical mechanics OurBigBook.com
The period is the time required for a periodic motion to complete one full cycle.

Force

Words: 122 Articles: 5
Classical mechanics OurBigBook.com
A force is an interaction that changes momentum; in Newtonian mechanics it satisfies F=ma for constant mass.

Force balance

Words: 34
Force OurBigBook.com
Force balance equates the rate of change of momentum to the sum of applied forces. A static continuum segment with internal resultant F(s) and force density f(s) obeys ∂s​F+f=0.

Newton's first law

Words: 18
Force OurBigBook.com
In an inertial frame, a body subject to no net force remains at rest or moves with constant velocity.

Newton's second law

Words: 14
Force OurBigBook.com
The net force equals the time derivative of momentum; for constant mass, F=ma.

Newton's third law

Words: 27
Force OurBigBook.com
For an isolated pair of particles, the force of particle 1 on particle 2 is equal and opposite to the force of particle 2 on particle 1.

Normal force

Words: 12
Force OurBigBook.com
A normal force is a contact force perpendicular to the constraining surface.

For a frame rotating with constant angular velocity ω,
ainertial​=x¨+2ω×x˙+ω×(ω×x).
(9)

Circular motion

Uniform circular motion of radius a and angular frequency ω has centripetal acceleration of magnitude aω2 toward the centre.

Circular orbit

Circular motion OurBigBook.com
A circular orbit maintains constant distance from its centre of attraction. Its inward radial acceleration has magnitude v2/r, so the radial force must satisfy Fr​=−mv2/r.

p=mc∣x˙∣x˙​,∣p∣=mc,H=V(x).

Gravitational radius (Rg​)

Words: 33
Virial theorem OurBigBook.com

Rg​=−WGM2​.
(14)
It converts the total binding energy into a characteristic size without assuming a particular density profile.

Hamiltonian mechanics OurBigBook.com
The leapfrog integrator alternates half-steps for momentum with a full step for position and a final momentum half-step. It is reversible, symplectic, and second-order accurate.

Hamiltonian flow

Words: 12

Hamiltonian flow is the phase-space evolution generated by Hamilton's equations for a fixed Hamiltonian.

Integral of motion

Hamiltonian mechanics OurBigBook.com
An integral of motion is a function on phase space that remains constant along every trajectory. If it has no explicit time dependence, I(q,p) is an integral exactly when its Poisson bracket with the Hamiltonian vanishes: {I,H}=0.

Conserved quantity

Words: 30
Integral of motion OurBigBook.com
A conserved quantity is a quantity that remains constant along the time evolution of a system. In Hamiltonian mechanics, a possibly time-dependent phase-space function F is conserved exactly when ∂t​F+{F,H}=0.
